sources.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs — quoted full-text passages (arXiv 2311.17371v3 PDF)

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors benchmark several multi-agent debate (MAD) and prompting strategies for trade-offs between cost, time and accuracy and find that MAD systems in their current form do not reliably outperform other prompting strategies such as self-consistency and ensembling over multiple reasoning paths. They report that with hyperparameter tuning some MAD systems such as Multi-Persona do better, suggesting MAD is more sensitive to hyperparameters rather than inherently worse, and that adjusting agent agreement levels can surpass all non-debate protocols they evaluated.
title: Benchmark: multi-agent debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling
